//: Canonical public-API vocabulary for al-* components. Enforced by scripts/check-api-vocabulary.mjs; explained in .altitude/API-VOCABULARY.md. A property is judged in one of four ways: a RESERVED name is always a violation (it hides which axis it means); an AXIS name must declare values drawn from that axis's set; a BOOLEAN must carry an allowed prefix or be a standard HTML boolean attribute; everything else is free-form and carries no opinion. `exceptions` is a debt ledger, not a permission list -- every entry is counted by the ratchet in .altitude/baselines/api-vocabulary.json, so the ledger can only shrink.

emphasis.means: Visual weight within one component's own hierarchy. Never carries meaning about state.

status.means: Semantic state the user must read. One set across every component that has one.

size.means: One t-shirt scale. A component may use a subset, never a different spelling.

position.means: Where a floating or attached element is anchored relative to its trigger.

direction.means: Flow of a component's own children along the main axis.

orientation.means: The axis a single element is drawn along (a rule, a stepper track). Not about children.

align.means: Cross-axis alignment of children. NOT anchored placement -- that is `position`.

reserved.variant: Ambiguous: across the library it already means emphasis, status, size, orientation, shape, layout mode AND brand, so `variant="sm"` is a size on one element, invalid on the next and a status on a third. Name the axis instead -- emphasis, status, size, position, direction, orientation or shape.
reserved.alignment: Use `position` for anchored placement, or `align` for cross-axis alignment of children.
reserved.flyoutPosition: Use `position`. A prefix does not make a second placement vocabulary legal.
reserved.labelPosition: Use `position`. The subject is already the label; the prop need not say so again.
reserved.layout: Use `direction` for flow, or a named mode on an axis of its own.
reserved.color: Use `status` for meaning, or a token on the consuming side for decoration.
reserved.level: Use `size` for scale, or a domain-specific name (`headingLevel`) when it is truly semantic.

booleans.//prefixes: `is*` for a state the component is in, `has*` for a part it owns. Nothing else -- a `hide*`/`show*` pair means the same fact reads true on one element and false on another.
booleans.//bareAllowed: Standard HTML boolean attribute names only. A bare name is legal precisely because HTML already fixed its meaning.

exceptions.//: tag -> prop -> reason. Every entry is a KNOWN violation, kept green so the gate could land; every entry is counted by the ratchet. Add one only with the reason it cannot be fixed today, and delete it the moment it is.
exceptions.//hide-family: `hide*` inverts the polarity of the rest of the library -- `isLabelHidden` reads true for the fact `hasLabel` reads false for. Twelve elements share `hideLabel`, so the rename is one coordinated change across the form set, not twelve independent ones.

al-alert.variant: status axis spelled `variant`, and missing `info` from the set.

al-calendar.disabled: collides with the library-wide `isDisabled`; one of the two spellings has to go.
al-calendar.resetDates: bare boolean naming an action, not a state.

al-combobox.align: `align` used for anchored placement (top/bottom); that is `position`.

al-heading.variant: size axis spelled `variant`, with its own display-* scale on top.

al-layout.size: adds 'full' to the t-shirt scale; that is a container width, not a size step.

al-pagination.variant: size axis spelled `variant`, and spelled 'small' rather than 'sm'.

al-progress.showLabel: `show*` family, the inverse polarity of `hideLabel` elsewhere. Wants `isLabelVisible`.

al-select.align: `align` used for anchored placement (top/bottom); that is `position`.

al-spinner.small: bare boolean encoding a SIZE. Wants `size='sm'`.

al-stat.invertPolarity: bare boolean naming an action; wants `isPolarityInverted`.

al-time-selector-list.resetTime: bare boolean naming an action, not a state.
